neighbours.label: a word for going right to something without delay or steps (jump straight to, straight away, directly to, get right to it, without further ado)
fire: Many graduates go straight to work after high school.
We start straight away with the first exercise.
This button takes you directly to the checkout page.
Let's get right to the point of the meeting.
So without further ado, here is our guest tonight.
The bus goes directly to the airport from here.
He skipped the warm-up and went straight to the main lift.

quiet: Many graduates take a long break after high school.
We start slowly with a long warm-up exercise.
This button sits at the bottom of the checkout page.
Let's talk later about the details of the meeting.

He finished the warm-up and rested before the main lift.

short: going straight to it, no delay
notes: Card: ' straight' x5, ' to' x2, ' faster' x2, ' quickly' x2, ' before' x2, ' directly', ' ado'. Probes: ' straight' 1.157, ' ado' 1.083, ' to' in 'right to it' 0.815, ' to' in 'directly to' 0.787, ' away' 0.753; 'walk slowly to college' 0.034. A distinction. Near misses have slow or ordinary progress.
